items.title: Beyond memory loss: recognising dementia in primary care
items.summary: An estimated one third of older people with dementia in England remain undiagnosed. Rachel Daly, academy lead Admiral Nurse at Dementia UK, explains how primary care nurses are well placed to recognise the patterns that point to the condition and make timely referrals. Dementia rarely presents as a direct concern.

items.title: Role of the clinical nurse specialist in neuro-oncology: a UK review
items.summary: Background: Clinical nurse specialists play a central role in coordinating neuro-oncology care, yet care models vary. Aims: To characterise variation in neuro-oncology clinical nurse specialist capacity, team composition, responsibilities and training across the UK.

items.title: The emerging drug pipeline for neurological diseases
items.summary: The drug pipeline for neurology diseases has changed dramatically over the past decade. In this article, Sue Thomas discusses the changed landscape using examples and explores how neurology nursing roles have expanded and evolved as a result.

items.title: Differences between post-stroke seizure and post-stroke epilepsy: a clinical literature review
items.summary: Introduction: Stroke is a leading cause of epilepsy in older adults, accounting for more than half of new cases in those aged >60. Post-stroke seizure and post-stroke epilepsy are associated with increased risk of death and disability.

items.title: Government announces £33m investment in dementia research initiative
items.summary: The government is to provide £33m of funding focused on recruitment for clinical studies to test new treatments for dementia. The investment will be made through the Dame Barbara Windsor Dementia Goals programme, alongside funding from Bristol Myers Squibb, GSK and Gates Ventures.

items.title: An online learning resource in support of the recruitment of people living with dementia and their carers to research
items.summary: Although the number of people diagnosed with dementia is increasing globally, it is estimated that only 2% are engaged in dementia research in the UK. In part, this may be due to a lack of confidence on the part of health and social care professionals to discuss research opportunities.

items.title: Nurse prescribing in multiple sclerosis: delivering evidence-based care in line with guideline updates
items.summary: The treatment landscape for multiple sclerosis has changed significantly over recent years. Independent nurse prescribing has become an important component of many multiple sclerosis services, supporting access to therapies, medication review and long-term disease management.

items.title: Beyond the diagnosis: the impact of stigma on Black people living with multiple sclerosis in the UK
items.summary: Black people living with multiple sclerosis can face a double stigma, writes Natalie Diana Busari. First, from a healthcare system that does not listen and fails to communicate internally. Second, from Black communities culturally reluctant to discuss chronic illness.
